why.formula: Conformance: each category scores the share of its checks that passed, a near miss counting half, and their weighted average is 100. Quality: hierarchy 100, rhythm 96, roles 100, system 57, weighted average 90. The score is 60% conformance and 40% quality (96), less 2 per distinct open hard problem (half for a near shade) and up to 30 for the share of layers with one, at most 25 (0: 0 problems on 0 of 6084 layers). Waived layers do not count. Checklist items are not in the score, because no machine checked them.

quality_parts.basis: 8 sizes; the largest is 3.2x the body size of 17px.
12 spacing steps used more than once, from 2px to 56px; 1 used only once.
quality_parts.how: Space with steps used again and again: 1 value is used only once (32px).

quality_parts.basis: 15 palette colours in use; the accent shows, and fills 8% of backgrounds.
70% of colours, fonts and sizes through brand tokens; logo not used; components used.
quality_parts.how: Write colours, fonts and sizes as the brand's tokens, var(--name); place the brand's logo with brand_asset_use.

checklist.text: Keep website/editorial and desktop app role namespaces separate within this one brand. Existing web tokens stay canonical for site/docs; app-* tokens describe the same brand in dense native UI. Website body type is 18.8 px at a 1440 px viewport; app body type is 13 px at 100 %. Do not substitute one context's scale for the other or add font families.
checklist.how: No machine can check this. Look at a canvas_screenshot and judge it yourself.

checklist.text: App interface scaling is an explicit persisted user preference: 75, 100, 125, 150, 175 or 200 %; default and reset are 100 %. Scale chrome fonts/tracking, spacing, controls, panels, icons, small radii and responsive layout live from the 100 % bases. Device zoom, CSS viewport, panel geometry, input coordinates and screenshot pixels remain independent. Ctrl+Alt+Plus/Minus/0 changes interface size; Ctrl+Plus/Minus/0 remains device zoom.
checklist.how: No machine can check this. Look at a canvas_screenshot and judge it yourself.

checklist.text: User overrides remain explicit. Higher UI size (including 150 %) and the optional Omarchy accent follow the same base roles, never another brand or font scale. Omarchy accent is accepted only by existing contrast validation and otherwise falls back to Tomato. Preserve the shared baseline palette.
checklist.how: No machine can check this. Look at a canvas_screenshot and judge it yourself.

checklist.text: The operations heading keeps semantic line groups: “operations.” is a block; the audience is a block containing the two inline-block phrases “For your agent” and “and for you.” Desktop widths 1440–3840 have two copy lines; mobile widths 320/390 have three. Preserve phrases rather than inserting arbitrary line breaks. Bogen's preview-viewport component prop reproduces the same CSS clamps for its render host; it is not another type scale.
checklist.how: No machine can check this. Look at a canvas_screenshot and judge it yourself.

checklist.text: The footer wordmark “tomacco” stays one line. Its containing content element declares container-type: inline-size; font-size is calc(100cqw / 4.36), white-space: nowrap and overflow-wrap: normal. Measure actual content width after parent padding, never the viewport or 1800 px cap as a proxy.
checklist.how: No machine can check this. Look at a canvas_screenshot and judge it yourself.

checklist.text: Product demos are silent inline loops: autoplay, muted, loop and playsinline; no native player controls or added playback buttons. Production keeps preload="none", lazy source data-src and data-demo-loop. assets/viewport.js loads/plays at 15 % visibility, pauses offscreen or hidden tabs and keeps posters for reduced motion. Bogen stores real clip/poster assets and supported flags; its HTML exporter adds playsinline, but its canvas does not execute the production visibility controller. Code handoff must preserve that controller.
checklist.how: No machine can check this. Look at a canvas_screenshot and judge it yourself.
